scenes.text: Imagine walking into a local grocery store and seeing every tub of butter's main rival dyed a bright, Pepto-Bismol pink.
In the late 1800s, angry American dairy farmers panicked because cheap margarine tasted just like real butter and seriously threatened their entire livelihood.

To fight back, they successfully lobbied governments to pass bizarre laws forcing margarine brands to dye their product bright pink so consumers would find it completely unappetizing, while other states forced buyers to take home white, lard-like blocks and manually knead in yellow food coloring themselves.
This ridiculous food war lasted for many decades before these laws were finally overturned, so tell us in the comments if you would actually eat pink butter, and hit follow for more crazy history!
